test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the sample registration system, which of the following state has the highest infant mortality rate (for 2019)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Madhya Pradesh**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** has the **highest infant mortality rate.**
 
• In Madhya Pradesh, the** infant mortality rate is 52 in rural areas **an**d 36 in urban areas.**
 
• **It has the highest infant mortality rate (48/1000)** in the country.
 
• In the year 2019, the infant **mortality rate among boys in the state was 51 per 1,000 **live boys and **the infant mortality rate in girls was 46 per 1,000** live girls.
 
• Out of 1,000 live births in Madhya Pradesh, 26 infants die within the first seven days of birth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Uttar Pradesh**

 
• **In Uttar Pradesh**, the **Neonatal Mortality Rate (NNMR) in rural and urban areas was 45.1%** in** 2015-2016 **and **35.7% in 2020-2021.**
 
• The Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in **UP is currently 50.4%, while it was 63.5% earlier.**
 
• The **infection rate was 15 percent in children before the year 2017, while it is now 5.6%.**

**Bihar**

 
• The** infant mortality rate in Bihar** is now decreasing year after year.
 
• Th**e death rate has now come down to 27%.**
 
• The infant mortality rate in Bihar is 1% less than the infant mortality rate of the country.

**Chhattishgarh**

 
• In the year 2020-21, there has been a big reduction in the neonatal mortality rate, infant mortality rate and mortality rate of children up to five years in Chhattisgarh.
 
• Both **neonatal and infant mortality rates have come down by 23% and 18%.**
 
• There has been a** significant drop of 22% in the mortality rate of children up to five years of age.**
